question.text: Merkel belongs to this German political party, which is mainly opposed by the Social Democratic Party.
question.clue: This party's leaders Ludwig Erhard and Konrad Adenauer sparked an "economic miracle" in its country post-World War II, and it has participated in various "Grand Coalitions" with the Social Democratic Party.

swap.leadin: In order to crack this German code, Polish and British cryptographers designed mechanical devices called "bombes" [bombs].
swap.text: Name this supposedly unbreakable code that was finally cracked by codebreakers at Bletchley Park.
swap.clue: This device was combated by the bombe, a form of early computer.

question.leadin: Name these things associated with the unification of Germany.
question.text: Germany had been unified after various German lands had come together to defeat France in this war in 1870.
question.clue: One side in this war, though equipped with the chassepot rifle, was nevertheless defeated by troops led by Helmuth von Moltke, who overwhelmed soldiers led by Patrice MacMahon.

swap.text: The Weimar Republic was almost overthrown in this unsuccessful 1923 coup d'etat, which led to the imprisonment of Adolf Hitler.
swap.answer: Beer Hall Putsch or Munich Putsch
swap.clue: Its leader started it with the proclamation that "The National Revolution has begun" and this event ended after a brief firefight between insurgents and police in the Residenzstrasse.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Battle of Britain.
question.text: The Battle of Britain was carried out by this air force that was led by Herman Goring during World War II.
question.clue: This force's limitations were realized during Operation Sea Lion.

swap.text: Along with his chief of staff Erich Ludendorff, this general rose to prominence after leading German forces at the Battle of Tannenberg. This general later served as president during the final years of the Weimar Republic.
swap.answerHtml: Paul von Hindenburg [or Paul Ludwig Hans Anton von Beneckendorff und von Hindenburg]
swap.clue: This man was reviled by Hitler, who referred to him as "that old fool" and "that old reactionary" during his time as president of the Weimar ] Republic.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Germany's role in World War I.
question.text: This decades-old grand strategy involved sweeping into France through Belgium on the event of a two-front war with France and Russia. Its breakdown under Moltke's command at the Marne led to trench warfare.
question.clue: This German strategy, named for a former German field marshal, advocated sweeping through France, then transporting troops east to handle the slower-to-mobilize Russian forces.

swap.text: Beginning in 1872, Bismarck waged this campaign against the Catholic Church. Bismarck's Prussian Minister of Culture, Adalbert Falk, issued the repressive May Laws during this campaign.
swap.clue: This social conflict came to an end with the passage of the First Mitigation Law negotiated following the death of Pius IX ], allowing clerics to be exempt from some Prussian laws.

question.text: The Spartacists sought to establish a Soviet-style state in the place of this post World War I German government, which held power until the establishment of the Third Reich.
question.clue: The Spartacist League disbanded shortly after this government executed its leaders Walter Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg.

swap.leadin: This battle began when Russian commander Peter Wittgenstein attacked Napoleon's right wing near Leipzig.
swap.text: Name this 1813 battle which halted the advance of the Sixth Coalition.
swap.clue: The defender's left side was commanded by Heinrich Holk until reinforcements arrived from nearby Halle led by Pappenheim, who was later killed.

question.leadin: This man built on the methods of the Gottingen School in his 1829 book on the First Serbian Uprising, which directly analyzed accounts provided by the philologist Vuk Karadzic ("KAH-ruh-jitch").
question.text: Name this prolific German historiographer. This spurner of a teleological theory of history attempted to elucidate the shared experiences between various European nations in his History of the Latin and Teutonic Peoples.
question.clue: While opposing Carr's relativism, Elton defended the more traditional, "scientific" methods used by this German historian. This historian classified European peoples into "Teutonic" and "Latin" groups in an 1824 book.

swap.text: Anti-Nazi theologians like Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Karl Barth formed this Christian movement after the Nazi Party officially absorbed Germany's Protestant church. This movement's views were expressed in the Barmen Declaration.
swap.clue: The founding document of this group asserts that the Church is "solely property" of Christ and denies the "false doctrine" that considers it an organ of the State, a position held by the Reichskirche.

question.leadin: Antoine Alfred, the Duke of Garmont, only wanted reassurances that Leopold of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen would refuse the newly-vacated Spanish throne, but instead he got this.
question.text: Name this document detailing the aggressive behavior of Count Benedetti toward Wilhelm I, named for a spa on the Lahn river.
question.clue: Bismarck's purposeful release of this communication about a diplomatic exchange insulted the French and caused the Franco-Prussian war.

swap.text: Literacy rates improved rapidly in this European state that implemented mandatory education in 1763. An enlightened despot of this kingdom supported the reform of Catholic schools in its newly acquired province of Silesia.
swap.clue: It developed from a monastic state of the Teutonic Knights, and joined in union with the Margraviate of Brandenburg, giving it control of Berlin.

question.text: As early as 1834, this Friedrich List-advocated customs union of German-speaking states, excluding Austria, provided a common market over much of Europe.
question.clue: Karl Bruck advocated the entry of Austria, but this plan was halted by the minister of commerce, Delbruck.

swap.leadin: This man temporarily gave up his throne after he was forced to sign the Treaty of Altranstadt.
swap.text: Name this Saxon elector who regained his throne after the Battle of Poltava, and whose death led to the War of the Polish Succession
swap.answerHtml: Augustus the Strong [or Augustus II; or Augustus Frederick; or August II Wettin; or August Mocny; or August der Starke; prompt on Augustus]
swap.clue: Seeking the secret of transmuting gold, this ruler imprisoned alchemist Johann Friedrich Bottger ("BOOT-ger"), who instead developed the Meissen variety of porcelain.

question.text: Skorzeny was supposed to head this mythically-named program to conduct irregular warfare post-1945. Instead, he helped set up the related ODESSA network to help Nazis escape.
question.clue: This underground partisan network set up by the SS to resist the Allied occupation of Nazi Germany.

swap.leadin: After this man was able to escape the grasps of Frederick I of Prussia, who was trying to learn of alchemy, he was caught by Augustus the Strong.
swap.text: Name this man who, in collaboration with the scientist Ehrenfried von Tschirnhaus in the pursuit of alchemy, accidentally brought porcelain-making to Europe at the Meissen factory.

question.text: The Herero Genocide was largely the handiwork of this German commander, who drove the Herero into the desert after the Battle of Waterberg, poisoned their water, and encircled the desert with his soldiers so that they could not escape.
question.clue: This military figure responsible for much the genocide that killed civilians and soldier alike at the Battle of Waterburg.

swap.leadin: Goethe's dramatic rendition of his life has him say the phrase "Kiss my ass" when he told it to the Bishop of Bamberg.
swap.text: Identify this German hero and mercenary that is known for fighting in the Peasants War against the Holy Roman Emperor. He had a prosthetic hand.
swap.clue: This play about an iron-armed soldier whose nemesis Weislingen has him arrested. Weislingen is eventually poisoned on the orders of the beautiful Adelheid.
